remarks.name: Peter Steinberger
remarks.role: Polyagentmorous ClawFather. Came back from retirement to mess with AI and help a lobster take over the world.
remarks.text:
Two months ago, we started the mission to “build OpenClaw with OpenClaw,” and bit by bit, we moved everyone from using their local coding harness to using https://t.co/ZFauM82U4k - our shared agent that knows what everyone’s working on and orchestrates it all.

Multiplayer coding + infinite compute with nodes and cloud sessions has been a game changer for how we build.

Local harnesses feel like relics of the past now.
remarks.translation: 两个月前，我们启动了“用OpenClaw构建OpenClaw”的使命，并一步步将所有人从使用本地编码工具链迁移到https://t.co/ZFauM82U4k——这是我们共享的代理，它了解每个人的工作内容并统筹协调一切。多人协作编码加上节点和云会话带来的无限计算能力，彻底改变了我们的构建方式。如今，本地工具链感觉像是过时的遗物。

remarks.name: Amjad Masad
remarks.role: ceo replit. civilizationist
remarks.text:
The lesson from the Hugging Face Incident should be that RL with verifiable rewards is an incredibly powerful optimization algorithm that will produce increasingly weird and surprising behavior from LLMs.

The obvious miss here by OpenAI is that they should’ve been monitoring CoTs —  Something they themselves called out as a safety strategy more than a year ago.
remarks.translation: Hugging Face事件的教训应该是，带有可验证奖励的强化学习是一种极其强大的优化算法，它将使大语言模型产生越来越怪异和出人意料的行为。OpenAI在这里明显的失误是，他们本应监控思维链——这是他们自己一年多前就提出的安全策略。

podcasts.name: Latent Space
podcasts.title: 🔬“我们有语言基础模型，但没有物理基础模型”——阿尼玛·阿南德库马尔，布伦计算学教授
podcasts.originalTitle: 🔬“We have foundation models for language, not for physics” — Anima Anandkumar, Bren Professor of Computing
podcasts.excerpt: 几年前，加州理工学院教授、Accelerated Understanding联合创始人Anima Anandkumar着手开发首个基于AI的开源天气模型。在与该领域专家交流时，她遭遇了质疑。天气是混沌的，物理模拟很难，已经发展了几十年，并且需要超级计算机，数据根本不够。尽管有这些保留意见，Anima还是坚持前行并着手构建。不到一年，她的团队就开发出了FourCastNet，一个能与现有最佳物理模拟相媲美的预测模型。多亏了Anima及其后续工作，现在任何人都可以使用消费级GPU在短时间尺度上准确预测天气。在我们发布的约十五期科学类节目中，<a target="_blank" href="http://latent.…
podcasts.originalExcerpt: A few years ago, Caltech Prof. and co-founder of Accelerated Understanding, Anima Anandkumar set out to develop the first open-source weather model with AI. Talking to experts in the field, she was met with skepticism. Weather is chaotic, physics simulations are hard, have been developed for decades, and require supercomputers, the data just isn’t there. Despite reservations, Anima went forth and built. Within a year her team had developed FourCastNet, a predictive model that is competitive with the best physics-based simulations available. Thanks to Anima, and her follow up work, anyone can now predict weather accurately over a short timescale using consumer grade GPUs. In the fifteen or so science episodes we’ve released on <a target="_blank" href="http://latent.…
